h1: Landscaping and yard care in Esquimalt
cardSummary: Small older lots, big boundary hedges, stratas and community grounds near the harbour, with a root-zone tree permit rule.
intro: Esquimalt fits a lot into a small township: older family homes around Saxe Point, West Bay and Gorge Vale, apartment and townhouse stratas, village frontages, and churches and institutional grounds.

The Township’s Tree Protection Bylaw (No. 3076, 2022) needs a permit to remove or prune a protected tree, and also to work in its protected root zone, unless the work is exempt. That last part catches bed renewals and new paths as well as tree work. Read about [irrigation](/services/irrigation/) or [request a free quote](/free-quote/?area=esquimalt).
localRulesIntro: Esquimalt’s permit covers digging in a protected tree’s root zone, not only cutting the tree, so garden and hardscape work near large trees is checked as carefully as pruning.

localNotes.title: Esquimalt Tree Protection Bylaw
localNotes.text: Esquimalt requires a tree permit to remove or prune a protected tree, or to work in its protected root zone, unless exempted. The Tree Protection Bylaw (2022, No. 3076) defines which trees are protected.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Harbour and Strait exposure
conditions.body: Lots near Saxe Point, West Bay and the harbour face wind and some salt spray. Low, wind-firm planting tends to last longer on those edges.

conditions.title: Small lots and big hedges
conditions.body: Many older Esquimalt lots are narrow, with tall boundary hedges and tight side access. Work is often done by hand or with small equipment, and debris has to come out through the house side yard.

conditions.title: Shallow soil in places
conditions.body: Parts of Rockheights and the Saxe Point area have rock near the surface, which limits deep planting and lawn depth.

conditions.title: Regional water and stratas
conditions.body: Properties are on the regional supply, so the CRD lawn days apply, and stratas use the complex’s street address.

topServices.why: Older spray systems in small beds and community gardens often waste water, and drip conversions suit the drip-any-day rule.
Compact lots with mature hedges and small lawns need regular, hands-on visits more than large machinery.

jobNotes.title: Side-yard hedge reduced by hand
jobNotes.body: A tall boundary hedge along a narrow side yard was reduced with hand tools and the clippings carried out through the yard, with nearby trees checked against the bylaw first.

jobNotes.title: Mulched slopes at a townhouse strata
jobNotes.body: Thin-soiled banks at a townhouse strata were weeded and mulched on a monthly round instead of reseeded, since grass struggled over the rock.

cta.body: Tell us about access to the yard and any big trees nearby. Narrow side yards and root-zone rules both affect how the work is planned.
